title: Stabilize adaptive deadline smoothing to prevent tenant queue collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden regressions where short, latency-sensitive requests (<=64 tokens) experienced tail latency spikes and timeouts during mixed-length waves. Incidents correlates with increased long-context (>=8k) KV-prefetch churn and a recent adaptive deadline-smoothing heuristic rollout. Scope: observed on Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved pools), and in one Private upgrade window. ETA on impact spiked during ingress waves and maintenance-induced prefetch drains. Root cause hypothesis: the adaptive deadline-smoothing logic that extends admission deadlines for batches under heavy eviction pressure is aggressively deferring admission of short requests when long-context prefetch rates are high. Interaction between admission expiry timers, tenant-level inflight reservations and prefetch quarantine led to starvation of short flows: short requests are repeatedly deferred and miss the inflight window, amplifying long-tail latencies. Repro steps (synthetic): 1) Spawn mixed workload: 70% short request 30% long-context streaming requests with KV prefetch enabled. 2) Configure adaptive_deadline_smoothing to default rollout values. 3) Apply tight per-host KV memory constraint to force eviction churn. 4) Observe p50/p95 for short flows degrade while long flows maintain throughput. Telemetry evidence: - Spike in admission_deferrals metric and admission_expiry_count for tenant watchlist entries - KV eviction rate up 3x during incidents - Shortflow_served_rate drops to <30% of baseline - Correlated customer traces show repeated prefetch_handshake retries. Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-03): - Feature-flagged adaptive_deadline_smoothing disabled for affected clusters. - Emergency tenant-level shortflow_quota applied for two enterprise customers (hosted). - Deployed watchdog that force-accepts short requests when shortflow_pending_ratio > 0.6. Proposed permanent fix: 1) Modify smoothing algorithm to be length-aware: maintain separate sliding reservations for short and long request classes and ensure short-class reservation has guaranteed min admission tokens. 2) Introduce early-exit path for short requests: if shortflow_pending_ratio crosses a threshold, bypass smoothing and admit into a fast-path micro-batch. 3) Harden prefetch quarantine handshake to avoid eviction-triggered admission expiry races by adding hysteresis to eviction counters. 4) Add deterministic backoff to admission_deferral so requests eventually age into admission instead of repeatedly deferring (bounded retries). 5) Add new telemetry and synthetic canaries specific to mixed-length waves (shortflow_p50/p99, admission_deferrals_by_length, kv_evictions_per_tick). Rollout plan: - Implement behind runtime feature flag (adaptive_smoothing_v2). - Unit tests + integration tests on staging. - Canary on 5% of Hosted traffic and one Dedicated pool for 48 hours with monitoring alerts for shortflow_p99 > baseline*2. - Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with rollback on regressions. QA/testing: - New mixed-length load harness in infra: run 12-hour soak tests with various eviction profiles. - Regression tests for private upgrade windows to ensure no state corruption across rolling upgrades. - Add chaos test to inject prefetch eviction spikes and verify shortflow preservation. Monitoring and alerting: - New dashboards: Admission fairness by length, Shortflow velocity, KV churn correlation. - Add alert: shortflow_denial_rate > 5% for 10m. Post-deploy follow-ups: - Collect drifted trace samples and run automated quality-eval on outputs to ensure no generation regressions introduced by fast-path batching. - Run retrospective and publish postmortem. Customer comms: - Immediate acknowledgment to affected customers sent on 2026-03-02 with mitigation steps and ETA. - Promise for a technical write-up and a scheduled 1:1 with impacted enterprise accounts after stable rollout. Long-term: consider admission allocator redesign as part of Scheduler Reliability Initiative (Q3) to provide per-tenant SLO-aware admission and cross-tenant fairness. This ticket focuses on a surgical fix and telemetry to prevent recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: adaptive_smoothing_v2 behind feature flag implementing length-aware reservations
shortflow_p99 on canary clusters no worse than baseline*1.2 for 48h
no increase in end-to-end user error rates during canary
automated mixed-length soak tests added to CI with pass/fail gating
runbook updated and customer-facing postmortem draft prepared
